text.p: Shares in British brewer Bass Plc fell on Wednesday, extending Tuesday's fall as investors took profits after recent strength of the share price, dealers and analysts said.
By 1430 GMT, the shares were down 17p to 793-1/2p.
Dealers attributed today's decline to concerns over the Carlsberg-Tetley takeover and profit-taking after the recent rally.
"The shares have had a good run ahead of next week's results and there are still concerns of the Carlsberg-Tetley situation," said one analyst.
Bass initiated a takeover in August with Carlsberg-Tetley but still awaits a ruling by the Office of Fair Trading as to whether it is referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
The shares fell yesterday in a knee-jerk reaction to the 40 percent tax on alcoholic soft drinks announced by Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke yesterday.
"I don't think the alcopop tax is a particularly significant factor in today's fall," the analyst added.
The company reports full-year results next Wednesday.
